messages.author: 22d6bf0e16759db6
messages.subject: Exponential -> improper posterior
parts:
I'm trying out Stan for the first time and it's great so far. But I'm having trouble understanding why I'm getting an improper-posterior error for this trivial example:


data {
}


parameters {
    real theta;
}


model {
    theta ~ exponential(1);
}


It seems to work fine for

theta ~ normal(0, 1);

so I'm not sure what's going on.

This is Stan version 2.3.0, called using RStan; the error is precisely:

Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) :
  Posterior is improper. Please check your model.
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

Thanks much,
Ed

messages.author: 22d6bf0e16759db6
messages.subject: Re: Exponential -> improper posterior
parts:
Ah, I just added the constraint

real<lower=0> theta;

and everything works great.

My question becomes, then, does the original code behave as expected, and if so, why?

Ed

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Exponential -> improper posterior
parts:
The exponential distribution is only defined for positive parameters, but theta is not constrained
in your model.  What’s happening is that theta is randomly initialized to a negative value and the 
sampler can’t get started.

What you want is

parameters {
    real<lower=0> theta;
}

model {
    theta ~ exponential(1);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Exponential -> improper posterior
parts:
It's impossible to infer, in general, so we haven't tried
in particular cases. It might be worth doing something limited
if we could catch some easy cases.

What we really need to do in this case is print out the warning
messages. I'm not sure why they're getting supressed during warmup.
I created an issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/779

It's something we should be able to fix on the Stan side so that
it carries over to RStan.

- Bob
